types.name: FAnimSequenceCook
types.doc:
The cook of an AnimSequence package (ROADMAP §23.8 step 11). The editor form
keeps every key as floats in the `Tracks` chunk; the cooked form keeps each
bone track the way the runtime samples it — the engine's animation codec
(Animation/AnimationCompression.h, the same one the .mmodel clips use):

AnimChannels      one descriptor per Channel node, in payload order: per
track the format, key count, byte offset and the time
and value ranges the quantized words are fractions of
CompressedTracks  the keys — 8-byte quantized records (16-bit time and
axes, smallest-three 48-bit rotations), a constant track
collapsed to one key, and a track whose measured error
misses the tolerance kept as raw floats; a quantized
track that meets its tolerance with fewer bits is
bit-packed at the narrowest width that does (variable
bit rate per track, 3 to 15 bits per component)
MorphTracks       the blend-shape curves, moved out of Tracks
(`cooked_offset` on each MorphChannel)

`Tracks` is marked editor-only, so the strip that follows drops it. A track
samples straight out of CompressedTracks (SampleChannel): no float copy of
the clip is ever rebuilt at load.

types.name: FAssetPackageCook

The cook of a binary asset package (.mesh, .tex, .anim, ...), what `mbt cook` and
`mbt package` run over the staged tree (`MowoGame --cook-packages=<dir>`):
a Texture builds its mip chain for the target, and every package loses the
bulk it was made from (editor-only chunks). The result keeps its id, class
and imports, so every reference to it still resolves.

A cooked package is tagged `cooked`, and cooking one again changes nothing:
the staged tree persists across cooks and an unchanged asset is not
re-staged, so the same file meets the cook twice.

types.name: FBlockCompression
types.doc:
CPU block compression for the .mtex pipeline. With cook code compiled in
(MOWO_WITH_COOK) BC1/3/4/5 go through the vendored rgbcx and BC7 through
bc7enc, optionally followed by bc7enc_rdo's rate-distortion pass; a build
without cook code keeps in-house range-fit BC1/3/4/5 encoders (endpoints from
the per-channel bounding box, nearest-palette indices) and no BC7 encoder.
BC1 — RGB, 8 B/block (alpha ignored)
BC4 — R, 8 B/block (masks, AO, height: half the bytes of BC7 for one channel)
BC3 — RGBA, 16 B/block (BC4 alpha + BC1 color)
BC5 — RG, 16 B/block (two BC4 channels — normal maps)
BC7 — RGBA, 16 B/block (mode-based, near-lossless for most content)
BC6H — HDR RGB, 16 B/block (unsigned half; in-house encoder over all 14
modes, decode via the vendored bcdec — half-float API below)
Decompress is the exact CPU inverse — CPU fallbacks (thumbnails,
DecodeImageFromVFS) and the round-trip self-test run through it.

members.name: Compress
members.signature: static bool Compress(MtexCompression c, const uint8_t* rgba, uint32_t width, uint32_t height, std::vector<uint8_t>& out, float bc7RdoLambda = 0.0f)
members.doc:
rgba = width*height*4 source pixels; out is resized to CompressedSize.

The result depends on the image and lambda only, not on the thread count.

types.name: FExrDecode
types.doc:

scanline or tiled images (a mipmapped or ripmapped file gives its base
level), HALF / FLOAT / UINT channels at full resolution, stored
uncompressed or with RLE, ZIPS, ZIP, PIZ, PXR24, B44, B44A, DWAA or DWAB

multi-part files are refused with a reason naming what to re-export as — no

types.name: FFormatContract
types.doc:
The rules every binary asset format in this module already follows, stated
once so they stay properties rather than coincidences. Covered by the
format-contract checks in the asset-pipeline test.

**Little-endian on disk.** Every magic, length and offset is written in the
host's byte order and read back the same way, with no swapping anywhere.
That is correct today because every shipping target is little-endian
(x86-64, arm64 on both macOS and Linux), not because the readers are
endian-neutral - they are not. A big-endian target would need a byte-swap
layer, and this is the note that says so.

**Versioning is additive.** A reader accepts any version from 1 to
FORMAT_VERSION_CEILING and gates each block it did not always have on
`version >= N`. It must never reject a file merely for being older, and a
writer must never repurpose an existing field - a new field goes on the end
behind a new version gate. That is what lets a v2 engine open v6 content
and a v6 engine open v2 content.

**The magic is checked before anything else.** A truncated or foreign file
fails on the magic, so no reader ever computes an offset from garbage.

members.name: VersionCeiling
members.doc:
Upper bound every loader accepts. Deliberately far above the live
versions: it exists to reject garbage that happens to carry the right
magic, not to gate features. Raise it only if a format genuinely passes
it - never to make a rejected file load.

members.name: IsHostByteOrderSupported
members.doc:
True when the platform matches the on-disk byte order the readers assume.
The test asserts it; if it ever fires, the readers need swapping, not the
assert relaxing.

dropped. Assimp's own limit ran only when a probe parse had seen bones,

were trimmed.

the translator has already folded the source's unit scale and axis system
into the root transform (Assimp's GlobalScale and the FBX root rotation), so
the scene is in engine space: Y-up, right-handed, metres. A translator that
leaves that to the passes clears it and fills the two fields honestly.

moves. There is no per-vertex influence limit here — the limit is a pass

consumer that has a fixed slot count.

types.doc:

binds where is MaterialImportProfile's job, not the translator's: the profile
is shared by the cook and the live import precisely so the two cannot diverge.

the glass path, which a thickness of 0 switches off.

types.name: FMaudioImportSidecar
types.doc:
The import contract for audio, next to the format it cooks into. The editor
writes the Import block of `<source>.mdfmeta` through
AudioImporter::WriteSidecarSettings — still the only writer — and everything
that cooks a clip reads it back through here: the runtime's own cook, the
packaging cook, and the tests. The key names live here so a rename cannot
half-apply.

It sits in AssetFormats rather than Audio because the cook has to run in
tools that have no audio engine, no ECS and no physics; reaching up into

of them.

types.name: FMaudioLoudness

Integrated loudness to ITU-R BS.1770-4 — the measurement every DAW and every
broadcast delivery spec agrees on, so a clip a sound designer levelled to
-16 LUFS in Reaper measures -16 LUFS here.

The cook needs this because peak normalisation does not describe how loud
something sounds: a compressed voice line and a sparse footstep can share a
peak and be 12 dB apart to the ear. Levelling on the measurement is what
stops every new clip arriving at whatever level its source happened to have.

types.name: FMaudioOpusTable
types.doc:
The Opus payload of a `.maudio` (codec Opus). It is not an Ogg stream: the
runtime never needs Ogg's page framing, and a flat packet table is what makes
a seek one table lookup instead of a page bisection.

FMaudioOpusTable (16 bytes)
uint32_t packetOffsets[packetCount + 1]   relative to the first packet
packets, back to back

Every packet is one fixed 20 ms frame. Decoded sample k of the stream is
source sample k - preSkip: the encoder's lookahead delays its output, and
the decoder drops exactly that many samples at the head.

members.doc:

frames; decoding 80 ms ahead of a seek target and dropping it is what
keeps a seek or a loop wrap from clicking.

types.name: FMeshStreamCodec
types.doc:
The cooked form of a mesh package's render data (ROADMAP §23.8 step 11).
The editor's RenderData chunk is a whole .mmodel with 72-byte float vertices
(104 skinned). The cook splits it into separately loadable chunks and
quantizes the vertex streams:

RenderData.Rest     the .mmodel minus every range below (header, tables,
meshlets, skeleton, clips), zero runs coded as their
length — the char[64] names every table carries are
mostly padding
RenderData.Indices  every index buffer (base and cooked LODs), meshopt's
exact index-sequence codec; raw where it would grow
RenderData.Layout   where each range sat and how it was encoded
RenderData.LOD0     base-mesh vertices, quantized
RenderData.LODn     cooked LOD vertices, quantized — a streamer that wants
only the near LOD never reads them
RenderData.Sdf      the baked distance fields, verbatim
RenderData.Cards    the GI card sets, verbatim
RenderData.Morphs   the blend-shape targets and deltas, verbatim

A quantized vertex is 31 bytes (43 skinned, 6 position-only): position as
16-bit fractions of the mesh's own bounds, normal and tangent octahedral
16-bit with the tangent's handedness as a sign byte, both UV channels as
16-bit fractions of their own range, colour as half floats, bone indices
16-bit and weights 8-bit renormalized to sum to one. Decode rebuilds the
.mmodel the loaders already read, so nothing downstream changes; the error
is bounded by the steps above (half a 1/65535 step of each range).

types.name: MeshletDagResult
types.doc:
Full cluster-DAG for one mesh: meshlets of every level packed
into one flat array (level 0 leaves first, then each coarser level),
all indexing the SAME source vertex buffer through the shared remap +
packed-triangle arrays. The task shader selects a screen-space-error
cut through the levels at render time.

types.name: FMeshletDagBuilder
types.doc:
Nanite-style cluster-group DAG at meshlet granularity, built with
meshoptimizer: cluster → partition adjacent meshlets into groups of
~8 → simplify each group to half its triangles (border-locked, so
cross-group seams survive and a mixed-level cut stays crack-free) →
re-cluster the simplified triangles into parent meshlets → recurse.
Per-group errors are absolute object-space and strictly monotonic
(parent selfError > child selfError), and a group's children and
parents carry bitwise-identical group sphere+error, which makes the
runtime cut test race-free by construction. normals/uvs are optional
attribute guards for the simplifier (same weighting as the LOD chain's
FMeshSimplifier); pass nullptr for position-only simplification.

free.name: MMODEL_VERSION_CURRENT
free.signature: static constexpr uint32_t MMODEL_VERSION_CURRENT = 17
free.doc:
Current writer version. v2 added the node tree; v3 added the embedded
lights + cameras tables. v4 added per-mesh meshlet blocks so clustering
runs once at cook instead of every load. v5 widened the meshlet record
from 48 to 96 bytes with the cluster-group DAG cut fields (self/parent
group spheres + errors, level, group ids) — v4 files still load (records
expand to stage-1 semantics: level 0, infinite parent error, always
drawn). v6 appends a per-mesh baked signed distance field block (mesh-SDF
table + packed R16_UNORM distance grid) after the meshlet section;
v4/v5 files still load with no SDF block (HasBakedSdf()==false).
v7 appends the cooked discrete-LOD block (LOD table + packed vertex/index
blob) after the SDF section, so the runtime stops re-running meshoptimizer
on every load; pre-v7 files still load and fall back to CPU simplification
at hydrate.
v8 widens MmodelMaterialSlot with the surface truth the live import already
maps (opacity texture, emissive color, alpha-mask + cutoff, two-sided) —
without them a cooked model rendered foliage single-sided and unlit-emissive.
The header layout is unchanged; readers size material records by version
(MMODEL_MATERIAL_SLOT_V7_SIZE for pre-v8 files).
v9 compresses the animation block: each track carries a format byte plus
its time and value ranges, and its keys are written as 8-byte quantized
records instead of 16/20-byte float ones. A track whose measured error
exceeds the cook tolerance keeps the float records (format Raw), so no clip
is ever silently degraded. The channel record grows to hold the descriptors;
pre-v9 files carry the narrower record and are read as all-Raw, so old
content still loads and samples bit-exactly.
v10 widens the VERTEX record from 60/92 to 72/104: the tangent grows to a
float4 whose w carries the bitangent handedness (without it every mirrored
UV shell lit as if its normal map's green channel were inverted), and a
second UV channel is appended for lightmaps. Pre-v10 files load through a
per-record widening (see MMODEL_LIT_VERTEX_V9_SIZE) that fills w = +1 and
mirrors UV0 into UV1 - the values the old content behaved as if it had.
v11 appends a per-mesh GI card-set block: the surface cache's oriented boxes,
clustered offline from the geometry instead of fitted per instance from a
transform. Pre-v11 files leave cardMeshCount==0 and the runtime keeps the
single whole-mesh box it always used, so old content loads and renders
identically.
v12 appends a per-mesh morph-target block: each target's per-vertex position
and normal DELTAS against the base mesh, in the base mesh's vertex order.
Before it the format could not carry blend shapes at all, so every cook path
refused such a model and packed the raw source instead — which meant the
shipped game ran Assimp at runtime for any face, on Linux where Assimp has no
binary and on Android where it is a fatal stub. Pre-v12 files leave
morphMeshCount==0 and load exactly as before.
v13 widens MmodelMaterialSlot with clear coat, anisotropy and sheen
from the glTF material extensions, which the engine's surface
models render but no import path read, so such content lost its look.
Pre-v13 records read back as 0 (MMODEL_MATERIAL_SLOT_V8_SIZE).
v14 gives an animation clip its morph (blend-shape) tracks. The cooker
never extracted them and the clip header had nowhere to hold them, so a
facial animation worked in the editor's live import and was absent from
every built game. Pre-v14 clip headers stop at
MMODEL_ANIM_CLIP_HEADER_V13_SIZE and read back with zero morph channels.
v15 appends one float per cooked LOD entry: the simplifier's error as a
fraction of the source mesh's bounding-box diagonal. The cook measured it
and threw it away, so every mesh switched levels at the same global
coverage whether its LOD1 was lossless or had lost its silhouette. Pre-v15
files carry none and keep the global boundaries.
v16 lets a file store 16-bit indices: with MmodelFlags::CompactIndices set,
a mesh or cooked LOD of at most 65 536 vertices writes uint16 indices,
padded to a whole 4-byte word. Every index of such a mesh fits by
construction, and the index block was half the file of a typical prop.
Pre-v16 files (and v16 files without the flag) keep uint32 everywhere.
v17 names the morph target each clip morph track drives
(MmodelMorphChannel::targetName). A track keyed by index alone moved
whatever shape another mesh kept at that index, so a model whose morphing
meshes number their targets differently animated the wrong faces once
cooked. Pre-v17 records stop at MMODEL_MORPH_CHANNEL_V16_SIZE and read back
unnamed, which the runtime resolves by index as before.

free.signature: static constexpr uint32_t MTEX_MAGIC = 0x5845544D
free.doc: "MTEX" little-endian

free.name: MTEX_VERSION
free.signature: static constexpr uint32_t MTEX_VERSION = 4
free.doc:
v2: the reserved tail becomes streamingPriority (the editor already
round-tripped it through reserved[0]) + the mip-0 average color (linear
RGB floats) baked at cook. Same 64-byte header — v1 readers ignored the
tail, v1 files read back with averageColor zeroed and are detected via
version < 2.
v3: the mip-0 average ALPHA (masked-material coverage) rides bits 8-15 of
the flags word as unorm8 — the 64-byte header is otherwise full, and flag
readers test individual low bits so the packed byte is invisible to them.
v1/v2 files read back as averageAlpha = 1 (opaque) via
MtexAvgAlpha::Unpack's version gate.
v4: texture arrays and volume textures (MtexFlags::Array / Volume, depth =
layer or slice count, up to MTEX_MAX_LAYERS). Plain 2D and cube files are
byte-identical to v3 apart from the version word.

members.name: AngleThresholdDegrees
members.doc:
Faces whose shared edge bends by more than this are cut apart. 45 is
the hard-surface default: it keeps a curved run together and splits a
box into six charts without any hand-marked seam.

members.name: Margin
members.doc:
Gutter between charts, as a fraction of the 0-1 square. Two charts
closer than a texel bleed into each other under bilinear filtering and
again at every mip.

members.name: PreserveRelativeScale
members.doc:
Keep each chart at its world scale relative to the others, so a wall
twice the size gets twice the texture area. Off packs every chart to
the same size, which wastes resolution on small faces but maximises
the space each one gets.

members.name: Coverage
members.doc:
Fraction of the 0-1 square the charts actually cover. Low numbers mean
the shelf packer left gutters a smarter packer would have used.

types.name: FUvUnwrap
types.doc:
Angle-based charting with a planar projection per chart and shelf packing
into the 0-1 square — the same shape as Blender's Smart UV Project. Not
conformal: a chart that is not developable keeps the distortion its best-fit
plane gives it. For blockout, hard-surface and HLOD proxies that is the
right trade, and it is deterministic, which an iterative solver is not.

It lives here, below Game, so the HLOD cook can unwrap its proxies; the
editable-mesh tools in GeometryTools wrap the same code.
